-76.07270,36.82690.name: The New Hope Center for Reproductive Medicine
-76.07270,36.82690.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Robin L. Poe-Zeigler, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-1.16656,52.94112.name: CREATE Fertility Nottingham
-1.16656,52.94112.state: NG2 Business Park, Ground Floor, 17, The Triangle, Nottingham, NG2 1AE
-1.16656,52.94112.company: Satellite clinic to CREATE Fertility, Birmingham
-1.16656,52.94112.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. Satellite clinic to CREATE Fertility, Birmingham. A satellite is where patients are seen; the licence sits with the parent clinic, so the regulator's paperwork and the treatment are in different places. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-52.67915,47.58774.name: Northwest Atlantic Fisheries Centre
-52.67915,47.58774.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, June 2026
-52.67915,47.58774.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. A site of Fisheries and Oceans Canada. Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, June 2026. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-7.49000,53.27000.name: WuXi Biologics Ireland
-7.49000,53.27000.desc: A large biologics manufacturing site built in Ireland by a Chinese contract manufacturer. Where genetic medicines can be made determines who can get them, and that capacity is being sited according to tax, regulation and geopolitics rather than where patients are.

7.59450,47.55450.name: Syngenta — sustainability and regulatory reporting
7.59450,47.55450.desc: The company’s own published sustainability and regulatory disclosures. Self-reported figures are the industry’s account of itself, and having them in one place is what allows the account to be compared against independent measurement.

55.39000,25.09000.name: International Center for Biosaline Agriculture
55.39000,25.09000.desc: Research on crops that grow in saline soils and can be irrigated with brackish water, based in the UAE. Salinity already affects a large share of irrigated land and is spreading as aquifers are drawn down and seawater intrudes. Breeding for salt tolerance is the least glamorous adaptation work and among the most consequential, and almost none of it involves engineering.

-77.18000,38.74000.name: Defense Threat Reduction Agency
-77.18000,38.74000.state: Fort Belvoir, Virginia — 8725 John J Kingman Rd
-77.18000,38.74000.desc: Funds and runs US work on biological threats, including sequencing, detection and countermeasures, and pays for laboratory capacity in partner countries. Defence biology sits outside the civilian biosafety systems this map documents, so the same techniques are being funded twice over under two sets of rules — and only one set publishes what it approved.

78.49830,17.43990.name: Kaveri Seed Company
78.49830,17.43990.desc: Founded in 1976 and among the largest Indian seed companies, concentrated in cotton and maize hybrids across the south and centre of the country, with a research programme of its own rather than a purely distributive business. It sits in the group of domestic firms that sub-licensed engineered cotton traits from the multinational joint venture and then found the terms of that licence contested in court and capped by government. Reading this facet, the useful distinction is between a company that owns a trait and a company that owns the hybrid it is crossed into — in India the second group is large, organised and politically effective, which is not the case in most countries on this map.

78.49830,17.43990.name: Advanta Seeds
78.49830,17.43990.desc: Established in 1994 and now inside the UPL group, breeding rice, maize, sorghum and mustard aimed at low-input and high-risk growing areas, and operating well beyond India. The position is worth recording because this map documents mostly the opposite kind of company: a seed business owned by a crop protection multinational, selling into the smallholder segment that the four majors have generally not served directly. Whether that is a route into a market or a route out of dependence on it is exactly the question this facet exists to let a reader ask.

78.49830,17.43990.name: Advanta Seeds — igrowth
78.49830,17.43990.state: Hyderabad — one biotech centre and 20+ research stations
78.49830,17.43990.desc: The seed arm's herbicide tolerance technology, which the company states plainly is proprietary and non-GMO: it lets a farmer spray an imidazolinone herbicide over the crop for broadleaf and grass control without damaging it. That combination — the commercial function of a herbicide-tolerant trait, reached without genetic modification and therefore outside every biosafety register on this map — is the reason it needs an entry of its own. A reader tracking herbicide-tolerant crops through approval databases will not find it, and the field it is sprayed on looks the same either way. The company reports more than 60 crops and a pipeline above 850 varieties across those stations.

2.26900,48.88500.name: Bureau Veritas
2.26900,48.88500.desc: Founded 1828, listed in Paris, present in about 140 countries with roughly 82,000 employees and 2025 revenue of €6.47bn; its largest shareholder is the investment company Wendel with about 35.5%. It appears on every published list of the firms that test food and feed for engineered content, and on the lists of the firms that certify organic and non-GM claims. It bought a Chinese food testing company in 2019, and China had already become its largest market by revenue and staff two years earlier. A grower's certificate, a shipment's test and an importing country's compliance check are, in this sector, products sold by listed companies with growth targets — which is a different arrangement from a state inspectorate, whatever the standard being applied.
